title: The billing blow-up
customerLine: This is the third time you've overcharged me. I've been with you eleven years and I want a supervisor, now.
coachNote: A Caregiver's instinct is to apologize again and again, which loses authority with a Demanding caller. The guidance moves the agent into calm structure: what we know, what we've done, what's next.

title: Locked out before rent day
customerLine: I can't get into my account and my rent is due tomorrow. I don't know what to do, I'm really scared.
coachNote: A Fixer wants to jump straight to the account number. For a Distressed caller that feels like being ignored. The guidance slows the first 30 seconds: restate, validate, then one step at a time.

title: Which plan is right?
customerLine: I'm just not sure which plan is right for me. Can you go over the options again?
coachNote: A Sage naturally lays out every option with pros and cons, which freezes a Hesitant caller. The guidance narrows it to one clear recommendation and reassures them it can be changed later.

title: The storyteller
customerLine: Oh my gosh, you won't believe my week! So we were in Hawaii for my sister's wedding, and my card got declined right in the middle of the luau.
coachNote: A Diplomat can let a warm, chatty caller run the whole call. The guidance keeps the rapport but uses a friendly bridge back to the task, protecting handle time.

title: The fine print
customerLine: Which clause covers the early termination fee, and how exactly is it calculated?
coachNote: An Everyman's casual tone can read as unprofessional to an Analytical caller. The guidance drops the filler and speaks in exact numbers, policies and timelines.
